items.title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers

articles.title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
articles.summary: Pixel-space diffusion models have recently re-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with clean image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction). In this work, we revisit this choice and introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between $\boldsymbol{x_0}$- and $\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction across principal directions of the data, learned end-to-end with diffusion training. We find that the preferred parameterization varies systematically with the data representation and model capacity -- notably, increasing model capacity shifts preference toward velocity prediction. We evaluate MFlow across ImageNet, UCF-101 video, and large-scale text-to-image generation, demonstrating competitive or improved generative performance across diverse settings. In addition, we find that vanilla pixel diffusion transformers, irrespective of parameterization, retain a persistent high-frequency deficit relative to real image…

articles.title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
articles.summary: Pixel-space diffusion models have recently re-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with clean image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction). In this work, we revisit this choice and introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between $\boldsymbol{x_0}$- and $\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction across principal directions of the data, learned end-to-end with diffusion training. We find that the preferred parameterization varies systematically with the data representation and model capacity -- notably, increasing model capacity shifts preference toward velocity prediction. We evaluate MFlow across ImageNet, UCF-101 video, and large-scale text-to-image generation, demonstrating competitive or improved generative performance across diverse settings. In addition, we find that vanilla pixel diffusion transformers, irrespective of parameterization, retain a persistent high-frequency deficit relative to real image…

items.title: AlgorithmWatch kritisiert im Wirtschaftsausschuss: Weniger Effizienz bei Rechenzentren kostet die Wirtschaft Milliarden

articles.title: AlgorithmWatch kritisiert im Wirtschaftsausschuss: Weniger Effizienz bei Rechenzentren kostet die Wirtschaft Milliarden
articles.summary: Die Anforderungen an Effizienz für Rechenzentren abzuschwächen, wie es aktuell bei der Neufassung des Energieeffizienzgesetzes (EnEfG) im Bundestag debattiert wird, würde die deutsche Wirtschaft mit Milliarden Euro zusätzlicher Kosten belasten und Deutschlands Abhängigkeit von fossilen Energiequellen verlängern. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt eine heute veröffentlichte Studie von AlgorithmWatch gemeinsam mit dem Umweltinstitut München und dem Fraunhofer-Institut für System- und Innovationsforschung. Am kommenden Montag, dem 05. Oktober 2026, bringt Dr. Julian Bothe dieses Ergebnis als einen von mehreren Kritikpunkten in die Sachverständigenanhörung zur EnEfG-Novelle vor dem Wirtschaftsausschuss des Bundestags ein.
